anomalies.observed: Every VDD pin of both MCUs is on a single-pin unconnected net. FCC2 (STM32H753VITx) pins 11, 27, 50, 75, 100 and NAVC2 (STM32F405RGTx) pins 19, 32, 48, 64 are all isolated. The +3V3 net carries only MCU VBAT (FCC2 pin 1 is PE2 not VBAT; NAVC2 pin 1 = VBAT), I2C pull-ups, and connector power – no MCU VDD either. FCC2 pin 6 (VBAT) is also unconnected.
anomalies.expected: The specification states: '3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs.' All VDD pins of both STM32 parts must be connected to the 3.3 V rail (either +3.3V or +3V3, or both if intentionally split). Without VDD the MCUs have no core supply and cannot operate.

anomalies.impact: Both MCUs are completely unpowered. The board cannot boot, run firmware, communicate over any bus, or drive any output. The entire flight-control system is non-functional.

anomalies.observed: FCC2's 25 MHz crystal HSE2 pin 1 is wired to net NET0041 which connects to FCC2 pin 5 (PE6) and C110, not to pin 12 (PH0/OSC_IN). FCC2 pin 12 (PH0) sits alone on Net-(FCC2-PH0) with only C31 to GND. FCC2 pin 13 (PH1/OSC_OUT) is incorrectly placed on the VREF+_FCC net together with C14 and R59, while the actual VREF+ pin (20) is unconnected. On the NAVC side, crystal HSE3 pin 1 is on NET0118 with only C109 – it does not connect to NAVC2 pin 5 (PH0) at all; NAVC2 PH0 and PH1 each have only a 2.2 µF cap to GND with no crystal.
anomalies.expected: Both HSE crystals must connect to the MCU's PH0 (OSC_IN) and PH1 (OSC_OUT) pins with appropriate load capacitors, as stated in the spec: 'HSE crystal (both MCUs) ABM8G-25.000MHZ-4Y-T3' and the schematic notes 'High Speed External Crystal.' VREF+ (pin 20) should be connected to the reference voltage net, not left floating while PH1 is hijacked.

anomalies.impact: Neither MCU can lock to the external 25 MHz crystal. Even if power were restored, the system would fall back to internal RC oscillators, degrading timing accuracy for UART, PWM servo output, and IMU sampling – unacceptable for a flight controller.

anomalies.observed: The specification calls for two 'otter_CH330' USB-UART bridge ICs in the Connections sheet for programming/debug. No CH330 (or any USB-UART bridge IC) appears anywhere in the component list or netlist. USB1's D+/D- pass through 22 Ω resistors R45/R47 to single-pin floating nets NET0062 and NET0058. USB3 and USB6 have D+/D- completely unconnected. Only USB5 connects to the MCU's native USB peripheral (PA12/PA13 via R9/R21).
anomalies.expected: Per the spec: 'USB-UART bridges (programming/debug) | Connections | otter_CH330 ×2 | Connections.sch note "CH330 UART to USB Converters"'. Two CH330 ICs should sit between the USB connectors and the MCU UART pins, providing serial programming and debug access.

anomalies.impact: The board loses its UART-to-USB programming and debug interfaces. Users cannot flash firmware or access serial consoles through the two intended USB ports; only the native USB DFU path on USB5 remains (and even that is non-functional without MCU power).

parsed.summary: The design files contain critical connectivity errors: both MCU VDD pins are completely unconnected (no 3.3 V supply reaches the STM32H753 or STM32F405), the external 25 MHz crystals are misrouted away from the MCU oscillator pins, and the two specified CH330 USB-UART bridge ICs are absent from the netlist. Together these make the board entirely non-functional as a flight controller.
